ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

fix_commit_message:
avcodec/bsf/dts2pts: fix binary tree invariant violation on selective dec_poc

Modifying the keys of a sorted structure, be that a tree or other
can lead to changes in the ordering and undefined behavior.
It can also lead to collisions with existing keys.

All these cases need to be handled unless there is a bug elsewhere
that would prevent them.

Fixes: out of array access
Fixes: 504281984/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_BSF_DTS2PTS_fuzzer-6032368162111488

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 054dffd13368 on top of intro 2d241202fffd via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): In the HEVC support added to the dts2pts bitstream filter, hevc_queue_frame() needs to renumber (decrement) the POC of a subset of already-queued DTS2PTSNode entries stored in an AVTree keyed by (poc, gop) when a later-arriving frame reveals that earlier frames in the same GOP were numbered too high. The implementation used av_tree_enumerate() with a comparator (same_gop) to find matching nodes and a second callback (dec_poc) that directly mutated node->poc in place while the node was still linked into the tree being enumerated. Because AVTree requires that a node's sort key never change while the node is a member of the tree, this in-place key mutation during enumeration violates the tree's binary-search invariant, can desynchronize the enumeration walk from the tree's actual (changing) structure, and can create duplicate/colliding keys. OSS-Fuzz's DTS2PTS BSF fuzzer found this leads to an out-of-array access. Root cause: The code mutates the sort key of an AVTree node (DTS2PTSNode.poc, part of the (poc, gop) key used by cmp_insert) via av_tree_enumerate()'s callback while the node remains linked in the tree, instead of removing the node, updating it, and re-inserting it (with collision handling) as required by AVTree's usage contract.
